primitives.name: checkProfile
primitives.when: Use to gate which email an agent may act on: allowed senders, required checks, required body level, required link strength. Local and free, so re-evaluate it any time on the same record to replay a decision. It tells you pass or fail with the reasons; what to do about it is yours.
primitives.signature: checkProfile(record: Record|string, profile: { senders?: string[], checks?: { dkimAligned?, dmarc?, spf?, arc? }, body?: 'proven'|'partial'|'any', link?: Array<'signed'|'unsigned'|'none'> }, opts?: { at?: Date|number|string, parent?: string }) => { ok, failed: [{ rule, want, got }], record, rules }
primitives.fails: Throws `ERR_BAD_PROFILE` for an invalid profile (not an object, an unknown key, an empty `senders`/`link`, a value of the wrong type). Never throws for the record: one that is missing, not version 2 or junk fails the `record` rule (`record: null`).

primitives.name: hashDocument
primitives.when: Use to fingerprint a file the same way mailproof does, e.g. to compare against `record.attachments[].sha256` yourself. `mp.matchFile()` does this for you.
primitives.signature: hashDocument(bytes: Buffer|Uint8Array|string) => string
primitives.fails: Never throws on bytes or a string; throws a TypeError for any other input type.
primitives.example:
import { hashDocument } from 'mailproof';
hashDocument(Buffer.from('hello'));   // 'sha256:2cf24d...'

primitives.name: Mailproof
primitives.when: Start here. Construct one per trail (a git repo of records under `trailDir`), then `record()` each email you want a re-checkable proof of and `verify()` it later, offline. All methods are bound, so `const { verify } = mp` works.
primitives.signature: new Mailproof({ trailDir: string, trail?: string, resolver?: Function, otsBin?: string|null, stamp?: { mode?: 'batch'|'record', everyHours?: number }, now?: () => Date, trustedSealers?: string[], lockTimeoutMs?: number, worker?: { size?: number, cpuMs?: number, wallMs?: number, maxMemoryMb?: number }, content?: { store?: boolean, attachments?: boolean, days?: number, sweepDays?: number } })
primitives.fails: Throws at construction when `trailDir` is missing, `trail` is not `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`, or `worker`, `content` or `stamp` holds an unknown key or a bad value (`content.store` and `content.attachments` must be booleans, `content.days` and `content.sweepDays` positive integers, `stamp.mode` `batch` or `record`, `stamp.everyHours` an integer 1..720). Nothing touches the disk until the first `record()`. OpenTimestamps is on by default (`otsBin` absent means `ots` from PATH; a missing binary never blocks capture): pass `otsBin: null` to turn it off. In `stamp: { mode: 'record' }` the OTS stamp runs inside the writer lock and is cut off after `clamp(floor(lockTimeoutMs / 3), 5000, 30000)` ms.

primitives.name: Mailproof#attachment
primitives.when: Use to get an attachment of a recorded email back from the local content store (the sha256 comes from `get(id).attachments[]`). An attachment is stored once however many emails carried it.
primitives.signature: mp.attachment(sha256: string) => Promise<Buffer|null>
primitives.fails: Never throws. Returns null for a malformed hash, a store without attachments (`content.attachments: false`, or `store: false`), content that expired or was forgotten, and a stored file whose sha256 is not the one asked for (never returned). Takes no lock.
primitives.example:
const [a] = (await mp.get(id)).attachments;
const bytes = await mp.attachment(a.sha256);

primitives.name: Mailproof#check
primitives.when: Use for a one-off look at an email you were handed (a saved .eml), when you do NOT want it recorded. It returns both verdicts and writes nothing. Use `record()` instead to keep a proof.
primitives.signature: mp.check(raw: Buffer|string, opts?: { envelope?: Envelope }) => Promise<{ live, portable, signatures: number, unsigned: boolean, partial_body: boolean, key_errors: string[], body_status, body[] }>
primitives.fails: Rejects on an empty message. Unsigned or unverifiable mail does not throw: it comes back `unverified`. A message over an input limit is not parsed or verified at all, and no DNS is asked: `unverified`, `reason: 'over limit: <name>'` on both verdicts (`total_bytes`, `header_bytes`, `header_lines`, `header_fields`, `signatures`, `h_names`, `sig_bytes`, `mime_parts`, `body_line`, `body_lines`; or `time` / `memory` / `crash` when the worker backstop stopped the build or its worker died, see the `worker` option), `signatures` 0, `unsigned` false, `body_status` `not-checked`. The limits: total size 25 MiB, header block 256 KiB, 4,000 header lines, 1,000 header fields, 10 DKIM-Signature headers, 200 names in one `h=`, 16 KiB per DKIM-Signature field, 200 MIME delimiter lines, 256 KiB per body line, 500,000 body lines (SPEC Part B, Limits). Judged as of now, so a key that has left DNS appears in `key_errors` and the portable verdict is `unverified`. The portable verdict covers the signed headers only: read `body_status` (and `body[i].explain`) for the body.
primitives.example:
const mp = new Mailproof({ trailDir: './trails' });
const c = await mp.check(fs.readFileSync('mail.eml'));   // c.live.trust, c.portable.trust

primitives.name: Mailproof#checkProfile
primitives.when: Use to gate which recorded email an agent may act on, by id: allowed senders, required checks, required body level, required link strength. Same rules as the pure `checkProfile()`; this one reads the record from the trail first. Local, free, deterministic: re-run it later for the same answer.
primitives.signature: mp.checkProfile(recordOrId: Record|string, profile: { senders?, checks?, body?, link? }, opts?: { at?, parent? }) => Promise<{ ok, failed: [{ rule, want, got }], record, rules }>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `ERR_BAD_PROFILE` for an invalid profile. An id that is not in the trail gives `ok: false` with a failed `record` rule, not a throw.
primitives.example: const r = await mp.checkProfile(id, { senders: ['alice@gmail.com'], checks: { dkimAligned: true }, body: 'proven', link: ['signed'] }, { parent: requestMessageId });

primitives.name: Mailproof#close
primitives.when: Use to release the worker threads at once (a test, a long-lived process that is done checking mail). Workers are shared by instances with the same `worker` options, so they end when the last of those instances closes. Never needed for the process to exit.
primitives.signature: mp.close() => Promise<void>
primitives.fails: Never throws. `list()` and `copies()` keep nothing open between calls, so there is nothing of theirs to close. A call with nothing to stop, or with `worker.size` 0, resolves at once. With a worker (`size` 1 or more), a `record()` or `check()` still running when `close()` is called (or when the last instance sharing the pool closes) may reject, and if it rejects that message is not recorded: await in-flight calls before `close()`.
primitives.example: await mp.close();

primitives.name: Mailproof#copies
primitives.when: Use to see every route one signed message reached you by (direct, via a mailing list, forwarded), given the id of any copy or the shared `message_key`. `copies` share the key; `contained_in` lists other records that carry it as an attached original (forwards and list digests). `original` is the earliest `direct` copy whose body matched, or null. Use `get(id)` for a full record.
primitives.signature: mp.copies(idOrKey: string) => Promise<{ message_key, original, copies[], contained_in[] }>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `err.code === 'ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE'` when the `better-sqlite3` native addon cannot load on this platform (there is no fallback; `record`, `get` and `verify` do not need it), or `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` when bringing the trail index up to date had to wait for a writer longer than `lockTimeoutMs`, or `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (not converted: re-create it). Otherwise never throws. An unknown id or key, or a record with no `message_key` (unsigned mail with no Message-ID), returns just that record (or nothing) with empty `contained_in`. Answers come from the trail index (SPEC B5), a cache beside the trail that is opened and closed inside each call (nothing stays open, so `close()` has nothing to wait for): whoever can write that file can change this answer, never `get` or `verify`.
primitives.example: const { copies, contained_in, original } = await mp.copies(id);

primitives.name: Mailproof#counterparties
primitives.when: Use to see who is in this trail: one row per exact lower-cased address (bob@gmail.com and bob@company.com are two rows; DKIM proves an address or a domain, not a person), most recently seen first. `records` counts the records that name the address on From, To, Cc or Reply-To; `verified` counts the RECEIVED (`direction: 'in'`) ones among them whose live trust is `verified`; `first`/`last` are the earliest and latest `captured`. The trail's own owner appears too, on every record: a record does not say which address is yours. Then `list({ with })` for the emails.
primitives.signature: mp.counterparties(opts?: { limit?: number }) => Promise<Array<{ address, records, first, last, verified }>>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE` or `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` exactly like `list()`, and with a TypeError for a `limit` that is not a positive number. An empty or missing trail returns `[]`. Only addresses a record shows count (SPEC B8). Answers come from the trail index, a cache: not proof.
primitives.example: const people = await mp.counterparties({ limit: 20 });

primitives.name: Mailproof#expireContent
primitives.when: Use to enforce retention on demand; `sync()` already calls it at the end of a run, but only when the last automatic sweep is at least `content.sweepDays` days old (default 7; content therefore lives between `days` and `days + sweepDays`). Only content goes (raw emails, and attachment files no remaining stored email references): records, archived keys and git history are never touched, so every proof still verifies.
primitives.signature: mp.expireContent(opts?: { now?: Date|number }) => Promise<{ removed: number, attachments: number }>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` when another writer holds the trail longer than `lockTimeoutMs` (nothing is deleted; retry later), `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (not converted: re-create it), or a TypeError for a `now` that is not a Date or finite number. A missing content directory returns zeros without creating anything. A record that cannot be read, or has no usable `captured`, keeps its content. Idempotent. The scan of stored emails runs without the trail lock (writers carry on); the lock is held only for the deletions, so it is short whatever the trail's size. If the trail's history was rewritten during the scan nothing is deleted this round. Cost of the scan grows with the number of stored emails (SPEC B7).
primitives.example: const { removed, attachments } = await mp.expireContent();

primitives.name: Mailproof#export
primitives.when: Use to hand a counterparty the proof of what you exchanged with them (or with several of their addresses): a directory of the signed headers, signatures, archived keys and seals of every email that names one of `with` on From, To, Cc or Reply-To (a union), optionally within `after` (inclusive) and `before` (exclusive) capture time. Not the emails: no bodies or attachments. The recipient runs `verifyBundle` (or `mailproof verify-bundle`) with nothing of yours. It proves each record's signatures and seal, NOT completeness: you chose what to include. Run `stamp()` first so the seals are anchored; it never stamps or runs `ots` itself. Tell the recipient `bundle_sha256` by another channel so they can pass `--expect`.
primitives.signature: mp.export(opts: { with: string[], after?: Date|number|string, before?: Date|number|string, out: string, tar?: boolean }) => Promise<{ out, bytes, files, head, bundle_sha256, records, replies, keys, manifests, seals: { anchored, pending, unstamped, unsealed }, content: { stored, absent } }>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `ERR_EXPORT_EMPTY` (nothing matches; nothing written), `ERR_EXPORT_TOO_BIG` (over 10,000 records or 256 MiB: narrow with `after`/`before`), `ERR_EXPORT_EXISTS` (`out` exists and is not an empty directory you own, or is inside the trail, the content store or another bundle; an export never overwrites), `ERR_EXPORT_REWRITTEN` (the trail was pruned or restored while it read: retry), `ERR_EXPORT_SELF_CHECK` (the bundle did not verify, so it was not delivered: the trail is damaged), `ERR_EXPORT_TAR` (`tar` missing or failed), `ERR_STAMP_CHAIN` (a manifest chain that cannot be walked), `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` or `ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE` (from the index catch-up), `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT`, or a `TypeError` for a bad option (including an `out` whose parent directory does not exist). Read-only on the trail: it holds no lock while reading, makes no commit, runs no `ots` and uses no network; the bundle is built in a private temp directory next to `out` (mode 0700/0600) and moved into place, so a failure leaves nothing at `out`.
primitives.example: const r = await mp.export({ with: ['bob@example.org'], out: './bundle-bob' });   // r.bundle_sha256, r.seals, r.records

primitives.name: Mailproof#forget
primitives.when: Use to erase what you hold of other people's mail earlier than retention would: one email, a list, or everything with one correspondent. Only the raw email and attachment files not needed by any remaining stored email are deleted. The proof stays: headers, verdicts, hashes and archived keys still re-verify offline, and anyone who later produces the raw email (sha256 = the record id) or an attachment gets it re-checked.
primitives.signature: mp.forget(target: string|string[]|{ with: string, before?, after? }, opts?: { dryRun?: boolean }) => Promise<{ removed: number, attachments: number, dryRun?: true, ids?: string[] }>
primitives.fails: Throws a TypeError for a malformed id, an empty or non-string `with`, a bad `before`/`after`, or a bad `opts`/`dryRun`; `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` and `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` as `expireContent()`. An id with nothing stored is not an error (`removed` counts only what was deleted), so it is idempotent. The counterparty is found from the From/To/Cc/Reply-To lines of the signed headers in the record, of the unsigned record's `from`, and of the stored raw email's header block; the match is exact, `bob@gmail.com` is not `bob@company.com`.

primitives.name: Mailproof#get
primitives.when: Use to read one stored record (to export it, or to hand to `verifyRecord`). Use `list()` first if you do not have an id. In `addresses[]`, `signed: true` means some signature covers that header line, decided at capture; it does NOT mean the signature verified (read the verdicts, or the `coverage` of the `list()` rows).
primitives.signature: mp.get(id: string) => Promise<Record|null>
primitives.fails: Returns null for an unknown id or anything that is not 32 hex characters. Rejects only for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (`records/<id>.json`): `err.code === 'ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT'`, the trail must be re-created.
primitives.example: const rec = await mp.get(id);

primitives.name: Mailproof#linked
primitives.when: Use to read a thread around one record without trusting it blindly. `parents` are the Message-IDs this email names in In-Reply-To / References (`id` is the recorded email with that Message-ID, the earliest copy, or null when it is not in the trail); `children` are the recorded emails that name this one's Message-ID. `strength` is `signed` when a DKIM signature that verifies offline covers the header that names it, `unsigned` otherwise (a Microsoft sender signs neither). It reports what looks linked and never asserts "the reply chain"; the other copies of one message are `copies()`.
primitives.signature: mp.linked(id: string, opts?: { limit?: number }) => Promise<{ id, message_id, parents: [{ id, message_id, via, strength }], children: [{ id, message_id, via, strength }], more: boolean } | null>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE` or `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` exactly like `list()`. Returns null for an unknown or malformed id. A record with no Message-ID has no children. At most `limit` children (default 1000, oldest capture first) come back and `more` is true when there were others; a `limit` that is not a positive integer throws a `TypeError`. Answers come from the trail index, a cache: the strength is the one found when the record was indexed (re-grade one record with `checkProfile`).
primitives.example: const t = await mp.linked(replyId);   // t.parents[0].strength === 'signed'

primitives.name: Mailproof#list
primitives.when: Use to find recorded emails, newest capture first, optionally by direction or by counterparty: `with` is one exact email address (case-insensitive, no grouping: bob@gmail.com is not bob@company.com) seen on the From, To, Cc or Reply-To of the record (`role` narrows it to one of them), `after` (inclusive) and `before` (exclusive) bound the capture time. It returns summaries; use `get(id)` for the full record. Each row also says who and what (SPEC B5): `from` (the first From address, lower case, or null), `to` (every To address, header order), `subject` (decoded text) with `subjectSource`: `'signed'` when a signature that verifies offline and aligns covers the Subject line, `'claimed'` when only the sender's word is there (a signature that does not verify covers it, or, for mail with no covering signature, the Subject read from the stored raw email, which is not proof), null when there is none; and `addresses[]` (`{ role, address, signed, coverage }`, header order). `signed` keeps the record's meaning (some signature covers that header line, decided at capture); `coverage` is the strict reading: `'signed'` a verifying signature covers it, `'failing'` only signatures that do not verify cover it, `'none'` no signature covers it. Show "signed" to a person only for `coverage: 'signed'`.
primitives.signature: mp.list(opts?: { limit?: number, direction?: 'in'|'out', with?: string, role?: 'from'|'to'|'cc'|'reply-to', before?: Date|number|string, after?: Date|number|string }) => Promise<Array<{ id, captured, direction, live, portable, message_id, from, to, subject, subjectSource, addresses }>>
primitives.fails: Rejects with `err.code === 'ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE'` when the `better-sqlite3` native addon cannot load on this platform (there is no fallback; `record`, `get` and `verify` do not need it), or `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` when bringing the trail index up to date had to wait for a writer longer than `lockTimeoutMs`, or `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (not converted: re-create it). A wrong type for `with`, `role` (it needs `with`), `before` or `after` throws a TypeError. Otherwise never throws. An empty or missing trail returns `[]`. Records captured in the same instant come in ascending id order. Only addresses the record itself shows count: a signed record shows the headers its DKIM signatures cover (an unsigned Cc is not visible), an unsigned one only its From (SPEC B8). Answers come from the trail index (SPEC B5), a cache beside the trail that is opened and closed inside each call (nothing stays open, so `close()` has nothing to wait for): whoever can write that file can change this answer, never `get` or `verify`.
primitives.example: const recent = await mp.list({ limit: 10 });

primitives.name: Mailproof#matchBody
primitives.when: Use when the original email turns up later (a mailbox copy, an .eml) and you want to know it is the one the record signed. A match upgrades the record to a full proof (`full`). Leave `raw` out and the stored raw email is used (content store, on by default).
primitives.signature: mp.matchBody(recordOrId: Record|string, raw?: Buffer|string) => Promise<{ match, full, signatures[], reason? }>
primitives.fails: Never throws on a malformed record (non-array `signatures`, junk entries: `match: false`). Returns `match: false` for a different email, an unknown record, a message over an input limit (not examined, see `check()`) or a body altered in transit (mail exported by some clients is altered; `verify()` can still pass in that case). With `raw` omitted and no usable stored content (store off, expired, forgotten, or the file failed its hash check) it returns `match: false` with a `reason`.
primitives.example:
const m = await mp.matchBody(id, fs.readFileSync('mail.eml'));   // m.full
const s = await mp.matchBody(id);   // against the stored raw email

primitives.name: Mailproof#matchFile
primitives.when: Use to check that a file is the attachment recorded at capture time (its sha256 matches). The hash is self-recorded and timestamped; it is tied to the DKIM signature only if you also produce the body (`matchBody`).
primitives.signature: mp.matchFile(recordOrId: Record|string, bytes: Buffer|Uint8Array|string) => Promise<{ match, attachment }>
primitives.fails: Never throws on a malformed record (non-array `attachments`, junk entries: `match: false`). Junk `bytes` (not a Buffer, Uint8Array or string) also return `{ match: false, attachment: null }` rather than throwing. `match: false` for any other bytes or an unknown record.
primitives.example: const f = await mp.matchFile(id, fs.readFileSync('contract.pdf'));   // f.attachment.filename

primitives.name: Mailproof#proofParts
primitives.when: Use when "the email is valid" and "this attachment is the one recorded" are different questions. `email` is the offline DKIM re-check of the record (`ok`, `trust`) and its recorded `body_status`. Each attachment is re-hashed from the content store: `match: true` is the recorded bytes, `false` a stored file that is NOT the recorded one (damaged or swapped), `null` nothing stored to check (proof-only account, expired, forgotten): then use `matchFile` with a copy you hold.
primitives.signature: mp.proofParts(recordOrId: Record|string) => Promise<{ email: { ok, trust, body_status }, attachments: [{ index, filename, sha256, stored, match }] } | null>
primitives.fails: Never throws. Returns null for an unknown id or an unreadable record.
primitives.example: const p = await mp.proofParts(id);   // p.email.ok, p.attachments[0].match

primitives.name: Mailproof#prune
primitives.when: Use to drop old mail from a trail on purpose, for example to honour a retention promise longer than `content.days`, or to shrink a trail that has grown large: every record, reply-text record, OpenTimestamps stamp and stored content captured before `before` goes, and the trail starts with a prune notice that says what was removed. Everything kept is byte-identical and still verifies offline; only the commit ids change. It is an explicit, rare, never-scheduled operation: it rewrites history. The old trail stays as `<trail>.pre-prune-<date>` beside it (still holding everything pruned) until you delete it, or pass `deleteBackup: true`. Writers keep working while the pruned trail is built; they wait only for the short swap.
primitives.signature: mp.prune(opts: { before: Date|number|string, deleteBackup?: boolean, dryRun?: boolean, now?: Date|number }) => Promise<{ cutoff, noop, dryRun, previousHead, head, removed, kept, stragglers: string[], dropped, keysCarried, reverify: { ok, failed: string[] }, backup: string|null, content: { removed, attachments, error? }, timing }>
primitives.fails: Throws a TypeError for a missing or bad `before`, `deleteBackup`, `dryRun` or `now`, or an unknown option, before anything is read. `ERR_PRUNE_RUNNING` when another prune of this trail is running (at once). `ERR_SYNC_LOCKED` when a `sync` kept running for more than 31 minutes while the swap waited for it, `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` when a writer held the trail longer than `lockTimeoutMs` at the swap: in both nothing was changed. `ERR_PRUNE_CUTOFF` when every record is older than `before` (a trail with nothing left is refused). `ERR_PRUNE_REWRITTEN` when the history was rewritten while the pruned trail was built (run it again). `ERR_PRUNE_VERIFY` when the pruned trail did not match the old one (a bug; nothing was changed). `ERR_PRUNE_JOURNAL` when a crashed earlier prune left a state it cannot recognise (nothing is touched; see SPEC B9.4). `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a flat pre-M3 trail. A `before` that removes nothing returns `noop: true` and changes nothing (no rewrite, no backup). Records captured before `before` that sit after a later one are kept and listed in `stragglers` (only a prefix of history is ever removed, never a range in the middle); reply-text commits for removed records are `dropped`. The result's `reverify` re-checks every kept record offline; a record that does not verify is listed, never a reason to stop. The time is about quadratic in the trail size on git's side (minutes at 20,000 records); disk needs room for a second copy of the kept trail. After the swap the sync cursor follows the new HEAD (so the next `sync` does not re-record the removed mail), the content of the removed records is deleted, and the trail index rebuilds on the next `list`. A crash at any point leaves either exactly the old trail or exactly the pruned one: the next call that takes the trail lock finishes or undoes the swap. Removing the backup is the only thing that makes the removal final. With `dryRun: true` it runs the same plan and the same re-check of the kept records and returns the same summary (`dryRun: true`, `head: null`, `content` zero, `backup` the path it would use) without building, swapping or writing anything: HEAD, the working tree, the content store and the sync cursor stay as they were; it still takes the prune lock (so it fails at once with `ERR_PRUNE_RUNNING` while another prune runs) and finishes an unfinished earlier swap like any trail-lock holder.
primitives.example:
const plan = await mp.prune({ before: '2025-01-01', dryRun: true });   // plan.removed, plan.kept: nothing changed
const r = await mp.prune({ before: '2025-01-01' });   // r.removed, r.kept, r.backup
await fs.rm(r.backup, { recursive: true });           // when you are sure

primitives.name: Mailproof#rawEmail
primitives.when: Use to get the original bytes of a recorded email back from the local content store (on by default), long after the mailbox has deleted it: hand them to any DKIM tool, to `replyText`, or to an auditor. Nothing leaves the machine. The bytes are checked on every read: their sha256 must be the id, so what you get is exactly what was captured.
primitives.signature: mp.rawEmail(id: string) => Promise<Buffer|null>
primitives.fails: Never throws. Returns null for an unknown or malformed id, a store that is off or never held it, content that expired or was forgotten, and a stored file whose hash is not the id (a corrupt or tampered file is never returned; the record still verifies). Takes no lock.
primitives.example: const raw = await mp.rawEmail(id);   // Buffer or null

primitives.name: Mailproof#record
primitives.when: Use to keep a proof of an email (one record per distinct copy, marked `direct` / `relayed` / `forward` / `digest`): it stores the signed headers, the signature, the archived key, both verdicts and the body status (`body_status`: did the body match the signed `bh=`, with hints on what changed) as one git commit, and never the body in the trail. With the content store on (the default) the raw email and its attachments are also kept beside the trail, outside git, for `rawEmail()`, `attachment()`, `replyText({ id })` and `matchBody(id)`. Call it for every email you may need to prove later, including ones that fail verification (they are recorded as `unverified`).
primitives.signature: mp.record(raw: Buffer|string, ctx: { direction: 'in'|'out', source?: string, envelope?: Envelope }) => Promise<{ id, duplicate, commit, record?, ots?, content? }>
primitives.fails: Throws on an empty message, a `direction` other than 'in'/'out', `err.code === 'ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT'` for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (not converted: re-create it), a git failure (the tree is rolled back: only files this call created are removed), or `err.code === 'ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED'` when another process holds the trail's writer lock for longer than `lockTimeoutMs` (nothing is written; retry later). Never throws because the mail is unsigned or fails verification. A message over an input limit, or one the worker backstop stopped (see `check()`), is still recorded (committed, accept-with-flag) but never parsed or verified, and no DNS is asked: `unverified` with `reason: 'over limit: <name>'` on both verdicts, `signatures: []`, `body_status` `not-checked`, and only the `id`, `raw_sha256` and `size` taken from the bytes (`message_id` null, no attachments, `copy.kind` `unknown`, `message_key` null). This includes a header block over 256 KiB, which used to reject with `EMAXLEN` and record nothing. The id is the hash of the raw bytes: the identical bytes recorded twice return `duplicate: true` and write nothing, while a copy with any byte difference (a list footer, an added header) is its own record, linked by `message_key` (see `copies()`). In `record` mode an OTS failure or timeout is reported in `ots`, not thrown, and the stamp runs inside the writer lock, so it is cut off after `clamp(floor(lockTimeoutMs / 3), 5000, 30000)` ms. A content-store write failure (disk full, permissions) never fails the call and never loses the proof: the record commits and `content` is `{ stored: false, attachments: 0, error }`. If the commit fails, the content files this call created are removed with the rest. The raw email of a message over 25 MiB is not stored.
primitives.example: const { id, duplicate } = await mp.record(fs.readFileSync('mail.eml'), { direction: 'in', source: 'file' });

primitives.name: Mailproof#replyFacts
primitives.when: Use to learn what the people you wrote to answered, without interpreting it: pass the Message-ID of the email you sent (the request) and get one bundle per recorded inbound DIRECT reply (its In-Reply-To names the request, or the request is the last entry of its References; later messages deeper in the thread are not included), earliest capture first. `[]` means no reply yet. Every value is a string from a closed set or free text, so a rule engine can compare them exactly: `from` (lower-case), `fromDkimAligned` (pass: an aligned DKIM signature that verifies offline covers From), `link` (signed/unsigned/none: is the request in a signed In-Reply-To/References), `bodyProven`, `quote`, `trailing`, `firstLine`, `text`, `dkim`/`dmarc`/`spf`/`arc`, `live`/`portable` (trust levels), `commit`, `recordId`, `messageKey` and more (SPEC B10). Copies of one signed message are separate bundles with the same `messageKey`; mailproof never picks or filters, the consumer groups and decides (an approval rule: allow only when at least one distinct reply is green and none is red). Nothing is written to the trail; the text comes from the local content store, so an expired, forgotten or disabled store gives `text` and `firstLine` of "" with `textSource` "none".
primitives.signature: mp.replyFacts(opts: { messageId: string }) => Promise<Array<{ messageId, messageKey, recordId, commit, trail, captured, from, fromRaw, fromDomain, fromDkimAligned, to, toRaw, cc, ccRaw, date, dateSource, subject, subjectSource, dkim, dmarc, spf, arc, live, portable, link, text, firstLine, textSource, bodyProven, quote, trailing, attachments }>>
primitives.fails: Rejects with a TypeError when `messageId` is not a non-empty string, `ERR_TOO_MANY_REPLIES` when more than 200 direct replies exist (a flood; nothing is cut silently), and with `ERR_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE` or `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` exactly like `list()` (the lookup uses the trail index). An unrecorded request, an empty trail or no reply gives `[]`. A reply with no Message-ID has `messageId` "".
primitives.example:
const replies = await mp.replyFacts({ messageId: '<q-123@mail.example>' });
for (const r of replies) console.log(r.from, r.fromDkimAligned, r.link, r.firstLine);

primitives.name: Mailproof#replyText
primitives.when: Use to read what a person actually wrote in a reply they sent you, without the quoted history (the trap: a reply that quotes "Approve payment of $5,000?" is not an approval). Record the email first (`record()`, or `sync()`), then hand the same raw bytes to this, or just `{ id }` when the content store holds them (the default). `text` is the new text; `proven` is true only when the recorded body matched the signed `bh=` (`body_status` `matched`), so the text really came from that signed email; `quote` says whether a quote boundary was found (`found`), none was (`not-found`: the whole body is returned) or the answer is written inside the quote (`inline`); `trailing` says unquoted text follows the quote and was not returned. The stripper is the versioned, deterministic `mailproof-quote/1`: anyone with the raw email re-runs it and gets the same text byte for byte. Signatures are not stripped. Interpreting the text (approve or decline, in any language) is the consumer's job, not mailproof's.
primitives.signature: mp.replyText(raw: Buffer|string|{ id: string }) => Promise<{ id, text, text_sha256, text_bytes, quote, trailing, source, boundary, stripper, body_status, proven, commit, duplicate }>
primitives.fails: `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a trail still in the pre-M3 flat layout (not converted: re-create it). `{ id }` with no stored content (store off, expired, forgotten, or the file failed its hash check) rejects with `err.code === 'ERR_NO_CONTENT'`; an `id` that is not 32 hex is a plain Error. Rejects with `err.code === 'ERR_NOT_RECORDED'` when the message is not committed in this trail (record it first), `ERR_OVER_LIMIT` with `err.limit` set when the message is over an input limit or the worker backstop stopped it (`total_bytes`, ..., `time`, `memory`, `crash`; nothing is written), `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` when another writer holds the trail longer than `lockTimeoutMs`, or a plain Error on an empty message or a git failure (rolled back). A message with no text/plain part is not an error: `source: 'html-only'`, `text` '' and `proven` false. The committed record holds fingerprints and flags only, never the text, the body or the subject; the same message and stripper version again returns the text with `duplicate: true` and writes nothing. `partial` body status (an `l=` signed prefix) is unproven in v1. `proven: false` is normal for mail received at Outlook/msn from outside (Microsoft alters the body): the words are unproven while the signed headers still verify; receive replies whose words matter at Gmail.

primitives.name: Mailproof#stamp
primitives.when: Use to seal what was recorded since the last run: from a cron job for a trail filled by the Postfix pipe (`sync()` and `mailproof watch` already run it every `stamp.everyHours`, default 6), or after a bulk `record()` loop. Only one 32-byte hash of a manifest (a list of file hashes, no addresses, subjects or content) goes to the public OpenTimestamps calendars; set `otsBin: null` to turn the seal off.
primitives.signature: mp.stamp() => Promise<{ enabled, mode, ran, skipped?, manifests: Array<{ seq, records, replies, sha256, commit }>, stamped: number|null, unstamped, unsealed, upgraded, pending, error? }>
primitives.fails: With `otsBin: null` it does nothing and returns `enabled: false`. A missing `ots` binary, a hung calendar or any `ots` failure does not throw: the manifest is still committed and the result carries `error` (a missing binary says `ots not installed: records are not sealed; install opentimestamps-client or set ots: false`). Rejects with `ERR_STAMP_LOCKED` (another job is running), `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` (retry later), `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT`, `ERR_STAMP_CHAIN` (the committed manifest chain is broken: nothing is written) or a git error. Idempotent: with nothing new and nothing pending it commits nothing.
primitives.example: const r = await mp.stamp();   // r.manifests, r.stamped, r.pending; r.error when ots is missing or a calendar is down

primitives.name: Mailproof#sync
primitives.when: Use to record the mail in a mailbox you can log in to (Gmail with an app password, or any IMAP server with an OAuth2 access token you obtained), from a cron job or a one-off backfill, instead of piping each mail in by hand. The mailbox is only read: nothing is marked seen, moved or deleted. Run it again to pick up new mail; loop until `complete` is true to backfill a large folder.
primitives.signature: mp.sync(opts: { host: string, port?: number, user: string, auth: { pass: string } | { accessToken: string }, folders?: string[], sent?: boolean|string, maxMessages?: number, maxBytes?: number, tls?: { ca?: string|Buffer|Array } }) => Promise<{ complete: boolean, folders: Array<{ folder, direction, attempted, uidvalidity, reset, last_uid, seen, recorded, duplicate, over_limit, skipped[], bytes, complete, error }> }>
primitives.fails: Throws a TypeError for bad options, before any connection. Then it throws only when the whole run is pointless: `ERR_IMAP_AUTH` (login refused; the message never contains the credential), `ERR_IMAP_CONNECT` (server unreachable, or its TLS certificate did not verify: TLS is always on and certificate checking is never off), `ERR_SYNC_LOCKED` (another `sync` on this trail is running: it fails at once, so a cron job skips an overlapping run). A problem in one folder lands in that folder's `error` (`ERR_IMAP_NO_FOLDER`, `ERR_IMAP_NO_SENT`, `ERR_IMAP_PROTOCOL`, `ERR_IMAP_TIMEOUT`, `ERR_IMAP_THROTTLED`, `ERR_IMAP_UIDVALIDITY`) and the run goes on to the next folder. The first trail error (`ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` or any `record()` failure) stops the run: that folder carries the error, later folders come back `attempted: false`, and progress already recorded stays recorded. It never throws because a message is unsigned, fails verification or is over a limit: those are recorded `unverified`. A message over 25 MiB is stream-hashed and recorded `over limit: total_bytes`; over 128 MiB it is listed in `skipped` and not recorded. Caps per folder per run: 1,000 messages and 512 MiB (`maxMessages` and `maxBytes` can only lower them), 30 minutes per call. A caller passes the secret only to `sync`; it is never logged, returned or stored. A restored or replaced trail is detected from the cursor file (`reset: 'trail'`) and rescanned automatically (duplicates are no-ops); no manual step. The run ends with the automatic stamp job when due (`result.stamp`, SPEC B13.1.7): one manifest and one `ots stamp` per due run, never one per message, so a backfill needs no special setting; a stamp problem never fails the run.
primitives.example:
const res = await mp.sync({ host: 'imap.gmail.com', user: 'you@gmail.com', auth: { pass: process.env.APP_PASSWORD } });
// res.complete, res.folders[0].recorded; call again until res.complete is true

primitives.name: Mailproof#upgradeStamps
primitives.when: Use on a trail created with `otsBin`, some hours after the records were captured: a fresh stamp only says "submitted to the calendars", and `ots upgrade` merges the Bitcoin attestation once it exists, so the proof then holds offline. Each stamp that gained it is committed as its own small commit; `sync` consumers call this at the end of a run, a `record()`-only consumer calls it from its own schedule. It asks only about stamps not yet known to be anchored (remembered in a sidecar file beside the trail, a cache), so the cost follows the pending ones.
primitives.signature: mp.upgradeStamps() => Promise<{ enabled: boolean, upgraded: number, pending: number, error?: string }>
primitives.fails: With no `otsBin` it does nothing and returns `{ enabled: false, upgraded: 0, pending: 0 }`. A missing or hanging `ots` binary does not throw: the pass stops and the result carries `error` (`ots not found`, `ots timeout`, ...), with `pending` counting every stamp still not anchored. `ots upgrade` exiting non-zero for a stamp the calendars have not finished is normal (it stays pending). It runs under the stamp lock, which is fail-fast: it rejects at once with `ERR_STAMP_LOCKED` when a stamp job or another upgrade is running. `ots` runs on a scratch copy of each proof with no trail lock held (at most 30 s per proof, `STAMP_OTS_TIMEOUT_MS`; the pass stops after 10 minutes and the next call continues); the trail lock is taken only to commit a proof that changed (one short window per changed proof, waiting up to `lockTimeoutMs`), so it rejects with `ERR_TRAIL_LOCKED` only when a writer held the trail longer than that (retry later). Also rejects with `ERR_TRAIL_LAYOUT` for a flat pre-M3 trail, or a git error if a changed proof cannot be committed (the file is restored). Idempotent.
primitives.example: const { upgraded, pending } = await mp.upgradeStamps();

primitives.name: Mailproof#verify
primitives.when: Use to re-check a recorded email later, offline, from the record alone (no DNS, no raw email). It judges `x=`/`t=` as of capture time, so a valid record stays valid after the signature's expiry. Pass `at` only to ask "was it valid at T?".
primitives.signature: mp.verify(recordOrId: Record|string, opts?: { at?: Date|number|string }) => Promise<{ ok, trust, basis, at, engine, signatures[] }>
primitives.fails: Never throws. An unknown id, junk input, a tampered record or a missing or garbled `captured` comes back `ok: false` (fail closed). `ok` means at least one signature verifies; `trust` is the portable level recomputed now.
primitives.example:
const v = await mp.verify(id);
if (v.ok && v.trust === 'verified') console.log('signature holds against the archived key');

primitives.name: verifyBundle
primitives.when: Use on the recipient's side to check a pair bundle made by `mp.export()` with no trail, index, content store, account or network: it re-checks every record's DKIM signature offline from the record and its archived key, that the files are the ones the bundle lists, the manifest chain and each OpenTimestamps seal (`ots info`, local). `anchored` means the proof is for these bytes and carries a Bitcoin block attestation; the block header is NOT checked against Bitcoin (run `ots verify` for that). It never proves completeness: the owner chose what is in the bundle.
primitives.signature: verifyBundle(dir: string, opts?: { ots?: string|null, expect?: string, strict?: boolean }) => Promise<{ ok, failed[], bundle, expect, files, records[], chain, ots, counts }>
primitives.fails: Resolves for every bundle it can examine (a missing, damaged, tampered or hostile bundle is `ok: false` with the failed checks named, never a rejection); rejects with a `TypeError` for a `dir` that is not a string or not an existing directory, or a bad `expect`/`opts`. Writes nothing; never runs `ots upgrade` or `ots verify`; no network.
primitives.example:
import { verifyBundle } from 'mailproof';
const r = await verifyBundle('./bundle-from-alice', { expect: bundleSha256 });   // r.ok, r.failed, r.records[0].seal

primitives.name: verifyRecord
primitives.when: Use to verify an exported record with no trail and no instance: a pure, synchronous, offline re-check from the record alone. Reach for `mp.verify(id)` instead when the record lives in your trail.
primitives.signature: verifyRecord(record: Record|string, opts?: { at?: Date|number|string, now?: number }) => { ok, trust, basis, passing, at, signatures[] }
primitives.fails: Never throws. A record that is not version 2, junk JSON, a tampered signature, a swapped key or a missing or garbled `captured` returns `ok: false`.
primitives.example:
import { verifyRecord } from 'mailproof';
const v = verifyRecord(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('record.json', 'utf8')));
